newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says Angolan army invaded its territory.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says Angolan army invaded its territory.

text.p: Zaire said on Friday heavily armed Angolan army troops had invaded its territory close to Cabinda, sending local residents fleeing.

State radio quoted a presidential statement as saying thousands of traders and local inhabitants had fled the Zairean village of Yema, close to Muanda on the Atlantic coast and about 400 km (240 miles) west of the capital Kinshasa.
"In fact this village had been invaded since the beginning of the week by 1,400 heavily armed soldiers of the Angolan army," the radio quoted the statement as saying.

It said Angolan troops were also around Zaire's diamond trading town of Tshikapa, in Western Kasai Province, adding that the alleged invasion had prompted the United States to warn Angola against getting involved in Zaire's civil war.
"Today everyone knows that it is Angolan troops that attacked Zaire without justification and with no declaration of war," the radio quoted the statement as saying.
The radio said Zaire planned to appeal to the United Nations and had invited the U.N.'s special envoy for Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye to visit the affected region.

Angola has been increasingly linked to Zaire's six-month-old conflict. Regional analysts say the Angolan government has been supporting Laurent Kabila's rebels who are trying to topple Zaire President Mobutu Seseko who for years backed Angola's UNITA guerrillas.
Zairean rebels have seized more than half of the Central African country's territory and are advancing on the capital Kinshasa.

Zaire authorities have said they suspect rebels and their alleged backers will try to invade from Angola in a strategy aimed at cutting off Zaire's only port at Matadi and an oil refinery at nearby Muanda.
Industry sources said many shipping companies are now reluctant to use Matadi port and some have started diverting traffic to Pointe-Noire in neighbouring Congo.
